title: "This is why RAM is so expensive": Elon Musk reacts to AI-generated video of Jensen Huang dancing as Sam Altman, Tim Cook and others cheer
source_used: Primetimer (full text from the fulltext folder)
key_facts: On Sunday 4 Oct 2026 Elon Musk replied on X to a tweet featuring an AI-generated video of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang dancing as crowds cheered; Primetimer's headline quotes his reply as 'This is why RAM is so expensive'.

In the video, other industry leaders including Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai, Sam Altman, Tim Cook and Musk appear as fans cheering Huang, who dances to an AI-written version of Michael Jackson's 1982 song 'Beat It'.
The tweet was shared by @bqlsj, which claimed that Bilibili, the Chinese online video-sharing platform, had several parody videos, and said today's AI-generated videos are 'indistinguishable'.
RAM prices have risen significantly over the last few years; according to NZXT, a major reason is AI, with data centres absorbing large amounts of global memory production to build AI servers.
The increase is also attributed to makers such as Samsung and Micron prioritising HBM production over standard consumer RAM.
The embedded text of Musk's reply is missing from the saved article, so his words are taken from Primetimer's headline; the date of the original @bqlsj tweet is not given.
quote_evidence: In a post he shared on X on Sunday, October 4, Musk replied to a tweet featuring an AI-generated video of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang dancing as crowds cheered.
The tweet, which was shared by @bqlsj, claimed that Bilibili, the Chinese online video-sharing platform, had several parody videos.
According to NZXT, one major reason for the increase in RAM prices is AI, with data centers absorbing large amounts of global memory production to build powerful AI servers.
why_it_matters_hint: A joke from Musk that ties AI to rising RAM prices, with NZXT cited for AI demand as a major cause.
event_date: Sunday 4 Oct 2026 (Musk's reply); date of the original tweet not given
